Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Compares — Zero2Repo benchmark of 17 from-scratch repository-construction tasks in six languages, built by a language-agnostic, LLM-assisted authoring pipeline with execution and adversarial validation; 18 model–harness configurations compared on the public leaderboard

No SDD approach evaluated. Harnesses: Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor (CLI versions not published). Configurations (model / harness): GPT-6 Astra / Codex and OpenCode; Claude Opus 5.5 / OpenCode and Claude Code; Claude Sonnet 5.5 / Claude Code and OpenCode; GPT-6 Sol / Codex and OpenCode; Gemini 4 Argon, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (1017), Qwen3.8 Max, Kimi K3, GLM-5.3, Hy4 Preview, DeepSeek V4 Pro, Step 5 Preview, Seed 2.1 Turbo / OpenCode; Grok 4.7 / Cursor. All with high reasoning effort. Runner: cbrun

Agent receives a product requirements document (Full_PRD.md, behavioural requirements grouped into feature points with normal, boundary and failure cases), an Interface Contract (package names, API and CLI entry points, argument conventions, return and error types), optional Hardware_Requirements.md, a build contract and an empty workspace with the toolchain installed. Deliverable: a complete repository in the native ecosystem with its packaging and build artefacts, plus a submit marker file

Solve: agent reads the PRD and Interface Contract, writes code, self-tests and revises in the empty directory within a 7200 s wall-clock budget, then submits by writing a marker file; denylist check (one correction attempt). Judge: workspace copied to a fresh offline container, hidden acceptance tests injected and run, binary reward. Task authoring: select and pin repository, build environment, reverse-engineer PRD and Interface Contract, write tests, neutralize names, verify, review and release
None during agent runs. In task construction, author inspection of each task after automated validation rounds (about one to two hours per task)

Tasks: 17-task release. Configurations: 18 model–harness pairs from the public leaderboard; four models run in two harnesses as separate sittings, not a controlled harness comparison. Baseline: none designated. Held constant: tasks, instruction text, high reasoning effort, 7200 s solve and judge limits, sealed hidden tests, blocked code-hosting and upstream packages, judging protocol. Acceptance tests: hidden suites validated by a reference implementation and adversarial validation; all-or-nothing reward, no LLM judge. Repetitions: one adopted run per task. Human intervention: none during runs

GPT-6 Astra + Codex best (15/17), Claude Opus 5.5 + OpenCode 14/17; bottom configurations 1/17; no configuration solves every task and task 014 is solved by none. Harness changes the result: same model in another harness differs by up to three tasks (GPT-6 Astra 15 vs 12, Opus 5.5 14 vs 11, GPT-6 Sol 9 vs 6, Sonnet 5.5 10 vs 9). Longer and costlier runs do not solve more (Opus 5.5 + OpenCode $195.69 for 14 vs GPT-6 Astra + Codex $80.57 for 15; DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 7 for $3.36). Of 306 runs 134 pass; of 121 judged failures 95 pass at least 90% of hidden tests; 51 unsuccessful runs never get a complete judge result. No significance tests

It separated the 18 configurations (15/17 down to 1/17) and distinguishes near misses from timeouts and missing submissions. Repeatability not measured: one adopted run per task, so run-to-run variance unknown and harness gaps mix harness behaviour with run variation. Limitations stated: small scale (17 tasks, non-Python results rest on one or two tasks, no language ranking), first 11 tasks from well-known projects likely in training data, Claude Fable 5.1 excluded, no per-test failure attribution

Limitations: 17 tasks, nine Python; first 11 seed projects well known, so pass rates probably inflated; one run per configuration and task, variance not measured; harness comparison not controlled; Claude Fable 5.1 excluded because it declined on safety grounds during construction; authoring pipeline not released; per-test labels not released. Gaps: agents fail by missing a few specified rules or by never submitting; RL with all-pass reward does not separate these defects; planned extension to 30–50 tasks, repeated runs, recent and private repositories

Inconsistencies stated by the authors: for Qwen3.8 Max, GLM-5.3, Step 5 Preview and Seed 2.1 Turbo the published configuration cost total does not equal the sum of per-task figures (and for the last two also tokens); Table 2 uses published totals; Hy4 Preview per-task costs shown as $0; some costs are OpenRouter list prices. Values from Table 2 and Figure 4; per-task sums of Table 5 (134 solved) match the text. CLI builds not published.
